source_text: An ille recogitabit eo tempore de deo positus illic ubi nihil est de deo? pacem, opinor, habebit in animo contendens pro auriga, pudicitiam ediscet attonitus in mimos. immo in omni spectaculo nullum magis scandalum occurret quam ille ipse mulierum et uirorum accuratior cultus. ipsa consensio, ipsa in fauoribus aut conspiratio aut dissensio inter se de commercio scintillas libidinum conflabellant. nemo denique in spectaculo ineundo prius cogitat nisi uideri et uidere. sed tragoedo uociferante exclamationes ille alicuius prophetae retractabit et inter effeminati tibicines modos psalmum secum comminiscetur, et cum athletae agent, ille dicturus est repercutiendum non esse. poterit ergo et de misericordia moneri defixus in morsus ursorum et spongias retiariorum. auertat deus a suis tantam uoluptatis exitiosae cupiditatem! quale est enim de ecclesia dei in diaboli ecclesiam tendere, de caelo, quod aiunt, in caenum? illas manus quas ad deum extuleris postmodum laudando histrionem fatigare? ex ore, quo Amen in Sanctum protuleris, gladiatori testimonium reddere, εἰς αἰῶνας ἀπ\' αἰῶνος alii omnino dicere nisi deo et Christo?
thought_title: The impossibility of godly thought at the shows
orientation: Tertullian is addressing Christians who attend the shows, asking whether they can possibly keep godly thoughts and conduct there.
pass_a_gloss: And will that man think about God at that time, placed there where there is nothing of God? He will have peace, I suppose, in his mind while he is contending for a charioteer; he will learn chastity, stunned, in the mimes. No, in every show no greater stumbling block will occur than that very more careful adornment of women and men. The very agreement, the very conspiracy or disagreement among themselves in the partisanships fans the sparks of lusts from their intercourse. No one, in short, when entering a show thinks first except to be seen and to see. But while the tragic actor is shouting, will he go over the exclamations of some prophet, and among the effeminate flute-players' tunes will he call to mind a psalm with himself, and when the athletes are contending, will he be about to say that a blow must not be returned? Therefore he will also be able to be reminded of mercy, fixed on the bites of bears and the sponges of the net-fighters. May God turn away from his own so great a desire of destructive pleasure! For what sort of thing is it to go from the church of God into the church of the devil, from heaven, as they say, into the mire? To weary those hands which you have lifted up to God by afterwards praising an actor? To give testimony to a gladiator from the mouth with which you have brought forth Amen to the Holy One, to say 'for ever and ever' to another at all except to God and Christ?

choices.why: Cultus here means personal adornment or dress, not worship; 'more careful' preserves the comparative force.
Conflabellant is a vivid verb meaning to fan or blow upon; keeping 'fan' preserves the metaphor of kindling desire.
rejected: blows up the sparks of lust

choices.why: Commercium here means social interaction or exchange between the spectators; 'intercourse' preserves the sense of mutual dealings.

choices.english: to be seen and to see
choices.why: The passive and active infinitives are deliberately paired; keeping the exact grammatical contrast preserves the point.

choices.english: into the church of the devil
choices.why: Ecclesia is deliberately used for the devil's assembly to contrast with the church of God; 'church' preserves the shocking parallel.
Caenum means filth or mire; 'mire' preserves the proverbial contrast with heaven.

pass_b_english: Will he be thinking about God at that moment, seated where there is nothing of God? He will have peace in his soul, I suppose, while he is rooting for a charioteer, and he will learn modesty while he is spellbound by the mimes. No, in every show nothing will prove a greater stumbling block than the very care people take over their appearance, women and men alike. The mere fact of being together, the shared partisanship or the rivalry between them over their sexual commerce, fans the sparks of lusts. In short, no one entering a show thinks of anything first except being seen and seeing.

But while the tragic actor is shouting, will he be going over the exclamations of some prophet? Amid the measures of effeminate flute-players, will he be meditating on a psalm? And when the athletes are competing, will he be ready to say that a blow should not be struck back? Then he could also be reminded of mercy while he is riveted on the bites of bears and the sponges of the net-fighters. May God turn away from his own people so great a desire for destructive pleasure!

For what is it to go from the church of God into the church of the devil, from heaven, as they say, into the mire? To weary those hands you have lifted up to God by afterward applauding an actor? To give testimony to a gladiator from the mouth by which you have uttered 'Amen' over the Holy One, and to say 'forever and ever' to anyone at all other than God and Christ?

problems.quote: will he be pondering the words of some prophet?
problems.why: Latin says he will retract (reject) the prophet’s exclamations, not ponder them.
problems.fix: will he reject the prophet’s exclamations?

edits.old: will he be pondering the words of some prophet?
edits.new: will he be rejecting the exclamations of some prophet?

fixed: Changed 'pondering the words' to 'rejecting the exclamations' because the Latin 'retractabit' means he will retract or reject the prophet's exclamations, not ponder them.

problems.quote: the shared partisanship or the rivalry between them over their social dealings
problems.source_quote: ipsa in fauoribus aut conspiratio aut dissensio inter se de commercio
problems.why: 'commercio' here means sexual commerce/intimacy, not social dealings; the context is lust.
problems.fix: the shared partisanship or the rivalry between them over sexual commerce
problems.ruling: Latin 'commercio' in context of 'scintillas libidinum' likely means sexual intercourse, not generic 'social dealings'; translation loses sexual sense.

problems.quote: will he call a psalm to mind
problems.source_quote: inter effeminati tibicines modos psalmum secum comminiscetur
problems.why: Latin says he will threaten with a psalm, not merely recall it.
problems.fix: and amid the effeminate flute‑players he will threaten with a psalm
problems.ruling: comminiscetur means devise/invent/contrive, not merely recall; secum implies plotting, changing meaning

edits.old: the shared partisanship or the rivalry between them over their social dealings
edits.new: the shared partisanship or the rivalry between them over their sexual commerce

edits.old: will he call a psalm to mind?
edits.new: will he threaten with a psalm?

fixed: Changed 'social dealings' to 'sexual commerce' because 'commercio' here means sexual intimacy, not social dealings.
Changed 'call a psalm to mind' to 'threaten with a psalm' because 'comminiscetur' means to threaten, not merely recall.

problems.quote: But while the tragic actor is shouting, will he be rejecting the exclamations of some prophet? And amid the measures of effeminate flute-players will he threaten with a psalm? And when the athletes are competing, will he be ready to say that a blow should not be struck back?
problems.source_quote: sed tragoedo uociferante exclamationes ille alicuius prophetae retractabit et inter effeminati tibicines modos psalmum secum comminiscetur, et cum athletae agent, ille dicturus est repercutiendum non esse.
problems.why: Latin states affirmative future actions (retractabit, comminiscetur, dicturus est) while English turns them into questions, altering the claim.
problems.fix: But while the tragic actor is shouting, he will retract the exclamations of some prophet, threaten with a psalm among the effeminate flute‑players, and, when the athletes are competing, he will say that a blow should not be struck back.

edits.old: But while the tragic actor is shouting, will he be rejecting the exclamations of some prophet? And amid the measures of effeminate flute-players will he threaten with a psalm? And when the athletes are competing, will he be ready to say that a blow should not be struck back?
edits.new: But while the tragic actor is shouting, he will be rejecting the exclamations of some prophet, and amid the measures of effeminate flute-players he will threaten with a psalm, and when the athletes are competing, he will be ready to say that a blow should not be struck back.

fixed: The source uses affirmative future verbs (retractabit, comminiscetur, dicturus est), so the English questions misstate the claim; changed to affirmative statements.

last_rejected.quote: he will be rejecting the exclamations of some prophet
last_rejected.why: retractabit here means 'recall/ponder,' not 'reject'; the point is he won't be reflecting on prophets.
last_rejected.fix: he will be recalling the exclamations of some prophet

last_rejected.quote: he will threaten with a psalm
last_rejected.why: comminiscetur means 'devise/mutter to oneself,' not 'threaten'; the irony is he'll compose a psalm inwardly.
last_rejected.fix: he will be devising a psalm to himself

polish.changed: Clarified the rhetorical questions so the reader can follow the contrast between what a Christian claims to practice and what actually happens at the shows, and made the liturgical allusion to the doxology explicit by keeping the quoted phrase intact.

notes.why: Gladiatorial equipment; reader may not know what 'sponges' refers to here.
notes.fix: Gloss: 'the sponges of the net-fighters (retiarii, who used nets and sponges)'

notes.quote: say 'forever and ever' to anyone at all other than God and Christ
notes.why: Allusion to the Gloria Patri or liturgical doxology is indirect; reader may miss the reference.
notes.fix: Gloss: 'say "forever and ever" (the doxology) to anyone other than God and Christ'
